main_body: Two-storey half-timbered house: a large shingled hip roof (rows 1-43) over a plaster and timber upper wall (rows 44-76) and a stone lower wall (rows 77-106)
top_band: At x=48, the roof slope is rows 1-42 in alternating brown #8f5c3f and dark #3b232b shingle stripes, then dark eave rows 43-51. At x=24 the left hip face has cream highlights in rows 2-4.
evidence: The roof is a large visible sloped surface with a hip on the left, so it reads as a top. A dark eave band (rows 43-46) separates it from the front walls, with an overhang line along the bottom edge of the roof. Below that are the timber-framed upper wall and the stone lower wall. Windows show dark inner edges and sills, so they read as inset. The structure matches the reference houses, so it passes as 3/4.

style.evidence: The piece has only 4 distinct colours, against 66 and 185 in the references. Median colours per tile are 3, against 11 and 18. Flat-fill coverage is 17%, against 0% for both references. The measured dark edge pixels are 100% neutral, against 7-9% for the references, so the outline is the sticker look. The roof shingles and stone blocks are drawn as two-tone patterns only, with no highlight, mid or deep steps. The plaster panels are large flat cream fills. This is much flatter and thinner than the references.
